meta.task: Independent falsification replication of maps/_labelaudit/LABEL_AUDIT.md and maps/_toolaudit/TOOLCHAIN_AUDIT.md
meta.replicator: independent verifier (no access to audit conclusions before deriving eigene numbers)
meta.privacy: pipeline/research_v196_scrub.py run over maps/_repl/*: 29 files scanned, 3 hits, all of them already-redacted markers (<REDACTED>) quoted from source data. No live credentials/tokens/IPs/repo-slugs/emails written.

A1.claim: Of the 91 rows research_v195_drift.py calls violations, N have tokens literally == 'NONE'; audit claims 63 (a large share).
A1.my_method: Loaded maps/v5b_label_train_{1,2,3}.json raw; copied toks_present() verbatim from pipeline/research_v195_drift.py; counted rows where toks_present(tokens)==False and grade!=NONE.
A1.detail: The counts are exact. The 'circular' characterization is HALF-right and half-wrong. (a) TRUE: research_v205_hybrid.py line 69 filters the eval set with toks_present(b['tokens']) and grade!=NONE -- the rule that builds the eval set is the same rule the audit charges with being an artifact. Also TRUE: the 63 literal-NONE rows are refused by toks_present() BY DEFINITION ('NONE' is in its reject list), so v195's 'violation' label on them is definitional, not empirical. (b) FALSE as stated: the counter-case is strong. An annotator writing tokens='NONE' while grading STRONG/MEDIUM is NOT obviously self-contradictory -- it means 'I found the record responsive but did not isolate a token string'. That is the annotator correctly recording absence-of-token while still applying judgement. So 'circular' mis-describes it as self-contradiction; the accurate charge is 'the rule re-reads the label it is supposed to test, so it cannot test it'. Of the 28 residual non-literal-NONE violations, ALL 28 are grade=STRONG with short-but-real tokens ('全绿','上线','部署','2/2','5/5') that v195's len>3 gate rejects -- i.e. a genuine len>3 defect independent of the NONE circularity.

A2.claim: The true no-evidence bucket is ~42 rows (3.7%), not 91 (8.0%).
A2.my_method: Four independent definitions scanned the work_log (never the tokens field), reading maps/v5b_train_data.json['work_log'], joined to bindings by pid. Definitions: D-A 'nothing artifact-ish at all' (no backtick span, no dotted-extension token, no n/n, no PASS/FAIL); D-B D-A AND no completion verb; D-C semantic content-word/artifact detector; D-D hand adjudication of D-A sample.
A2.detail: I reproduce 42 EXACTLY under D-A -- the audit's number is reproducible, but the criterion is wrong. Hand-reading the D-A 42 shows many rows plainly DO contain completion evidence: b2/b3 duplicate rows whose work_log is a finished '3月1日-3月22日版本更新公告' with a delivered table and sign-off; b2/WEAK '图标居中约束已经落地并过测试'; b2/STRONG 'no code diff' verdict with a 70/30 root-cause decomposition; b3 '我把局部裁切重新生成一份'. Adding a single completion-verb test collapses the bucket from 42 to 1. Sensitivity band: 1 (strict) to 42 (nothing-artifactish) to 197 (my six-signal tier-0) to 367 (any-of-six absent). The audit's 42 is the most permissive threshold they had and is an UPPER not lower estimate. The audit's own §3.3 line 'almost entirely b3' is right (b1 3 / b2 7 / b3 32).

A3.claim: Largest trustworthy subset = 122 bindings, cross-family consensus core, NONE = 0.
A3.my_method: Reimplemented the audit's construction from the source scripts: for each family with two annotators (v5b, v5c, v3), an ITEM is in the core iff, for every family that has A/B, A and B agree on the 3-class label AND the families agree with each other; require >=2 families.
A3.detail: Exact reproduction, including STRONG 33 / MEDIUM 89 and the fact that every core item is supported by exactly 2 families. IMPORTANT CAVEAT the audit under-states: v3_A/v3_B uses a DIFFERENT item pool (batch 'recheck') with ZERO pid overlap with v5b/v5c/clean_recheck (200 vs 200, intersection 0). So only v5b and v5c can ever form a >=2-family core; v3 silently contributes nothing to the 122 while the audit's §5.1 narrative implies three families. My v5b+v5c-only count is 123 (STRONG 34 / MEDIUM 89); the audit's 122 arises because load_set iterates set(da)&set(db) and the min(len)-indexed zip drops one binding. The 1-item difference is a real, small methodological artifact (index-matching instead of key-matching), but it does NOT change the conclusion. Conclusion survives: 122 (or 123) of 209 items, with zero NONE.

A4.claim: Noise ceiling raw 0.818 / kappa 0.622 (v5b_A vs v5b_B, 3-class, n=209).
A4.my_method: Aligned v5b_A/v5b_B by (pid, binding-index); mapped WEAK->MEDIUM (to3); computed raw agreement and Cohen's kappa with pe = sum_l (n_A[l]*n_B[l]) / n^2, labels {STRONG,MEDIUM,NONE}. Also recomputed with an alternative (pid,intent-prefix) alignment.
A4.detail: Exact to 4 decimals with the marginal-product (Cohen) kappa variant. Both alignments give identical results, so the number is robust to alignment choice. v5c 0.7703/0.5348 and v3 0.7538/0.2531 also reproduce. Note the formula variant matters in principle (weighted vs unweighted kappa would differ); the audit used unweighted, and it is correct for nominal 3-class labels.

A5.claim: strength3_train.json (1047 rows) is 100% single-annotator with pairwise-disjoint batches; whether train1/2/3 are 3 people or 1 person 3x is unresolvable.
A5.my_method: Compared pid sets across the three label files; inspected all metadata fields, mtimes, JSON serialization fingerprints, pid time-ordering, token/grade style fingerprints, and scanned intents for person-identifying markers.
A5.detail: Disjointness CONFIRMED exactly (0 overlap on all three pairings; 900 union). Single-annotator CONFIRMED (each file has annotator='train1'/'train2'/'train3', one binding-author per batch). The resolvability question: I DID find strong batch-level style signals -- token-field mean length 107.6 / 20.0 / 133.8, semicolon usage 181 / 0 / 359, literal-NONE 63 / 32 / 90, and disjoint date windows (b1 7 days, b2 13 days, b3 6 days all disjoint). But these are BATCH signals, not PERSON signals: one person annotating three different item pools on three different days with a shifting convention produces exactly the same fingerprint as three people. There is no per-row author id, no session log, no cross-batch calibration item. So I CONFIRM the audit's caveat: identity is genuinely unresolvable from these files. The style differences do, however, independently corroborate the 'measurement convention changed across batches' reading, and they would be a valid upgrade if a future file ever carried an author field.

B1.claim: The token table's false-negative rate is ~92.6% (audit calls it a lower bound).
B1.my_method: Imported program_grade() from pipeline/research_v205_hybrid.py (the object under test); applied over all 200 clean_recheck_200 items -> 27 NONE. Built MY OWN tiered evidence classifier (STRICT/MODERATE/LOOSE) independent of the audit's families, then HAND-ADJUDICATED all 27 rows by reading the full record, with an explicit rule: has_evidence=TRUE iff the record reports a completed action whose result is stated; FALSE iff advice/plan/feasibility/explanation/risk-assessment.
B1.detail: I reproduce the audit's arithmetic exactly (25/27 = 0.9259), and the same value under backtick-only -- which is the whole point: 25 of the audit's 25 hits come from ONE family, backtick_command, which matches ANY inline code span. That is a near-trivial criterion. Hand-reading all 27: only 9 (33.3%) report a completed action ([1] '已执行 npm install... 验证通过 pnpm -v 8.15.6'; [3] '我把 Setting.ini 的 menu_hide 改成 0 后，窗口变成 Left=1720'; [4] '已完成仓库检查' with git output; [5] '我刚实测' 187.19MB; [7] '已经帮你配好了' Run-key written; [8] NTFS dedup measurement; [13] '定位到了...我先删掉'; [19] '已设置完成 origin'; [0] '我刚做了对比'). The other 18 are plans/advice/feasibility/explanations ([2] layered plan; [10] '建议用强门禁实现'; [11] nullability norm; [16] Sentry setup advice; [21]/[22]/[24] CI config templates; [17] '我会用...技能来做'). The audit's regex precision on this population is 0.36. The corrected statement: the token table's true false-negative rate on this population is ~33% (9/27), i.e. the rule misses about a third of genuinely-completed items; the 92.6% figure counts every backticked plan as evidence. This is the single most damaged claim.

B2.claim: adjacent is anti-monotone (random 0.397 -> perfect 0.000), and 2 pipeline scripts still gate on adjacent.
B2.my_method: Reconstructed the real gold distribution from maps/strength_confusion.json (n=209, STRONG 58 / MEDIUM 147 / WEAK 4); swept a predictor forced correct on fraction a in {0.0..1.0}; recomputed exact/adjacent. Separately ran the audit's own gate-census regexes against the two flagged files.
B2.detail: The ARITHMETIC is exactly reproduced: adjacent 0.397 at random, monotonically collapsing to 0.000 at perfect exact, non-monotone at a=0.2->0.3 (0.316->0.373) and back down. That part is CONFIRMED and is a clean, correct result. The FOLLOW-ON is REFUTED: the audit's census flags _audit_f_ceiling.py and research_v200_adjacent.py as 'adjacent_used_as_gate' via the regex adjacent['\"]?\s*[><=] or adjacent\D{0,12}0\.9. Both hits are FALSE POSITIVES -- the matched text is 'adjacent=' inside an f-string print label ('exact={...} adjacent={adj*100:5.1f}%'), and the 0.9 match is a literal inside a print. Neither file compares adjacent to a threshold. Moreover, the real acceptance doc maps/MULTI_METRIC_ACCEPTANCE.md line 3 says the adjacent>=90% gate was RETIRED in §251. The actual gate research_v198_gate.py thresholds the REVERSE rate, not adjacent. Corrected statement: adjacent is anti-monotone (verified) and no pipeline script currently gates acceptance on it (the v1 gate was already retired).

B3.claim: Calibration leak: program rule scores 0.628 on train vs ~0.68-0.77 on eval.
B3.my_method: Imported the real program_grade(); applied to strength3_train rows (work-log part after splitting on the 【工作记录】 delimiter) and to v5b_A/B and v5c_A/B over clean_recheck_200; checked pid and first-120-char text overlap; then decomposed the gap by predicted class and by gold-NONE fraction.
B3.detail: All numbers reproduce exactly: train 0.6275, eval 0.6794-0.8230 (mean 0.7369), zero pid AND zero text overlap. I actively TESTED the alternative explanation (base-rate artifact: gold-NONE fraction is 11.7% on train vs 0-10% on eval, and the rule can never emit NONE-correctly... actually it does emit NONE). The gap SURVIVES the control: on the STRONG/MEDIUM-only subset (base rate neutralised) train is still 0.589 vs eval 0.679-0.820. The mechanism is visible: the rule over-predicts NONE on train (398/1047 = 38%) vs eval (28/209 = 13%) -- because train's work_logs are the ones that fed the drift/violation analysis that authored the rule. Direction-caveat: v205_hybrid.py (22:06) POST-dates strength3_train.json (21:48), so the rule was not literally fitted on the train set; but COVERAGE_CRITERION_v6_3class (21:48) was derived from the eval families' behaviour, and v209_indep_prog.py's own docstring states '§258 发现：程序 token 表由评估集标注反推'. The leak is real and the project itself acknowledges it. The quantification 'how much of the gap is explained by authoring-against-eval' cannot be pinned from timestamps alone -- I can confirm the gap is real and not base-rate, but not the exact attribution share.

B4.claim: 6/6 pipeline scripts use hand-written rules to judge labels with zero recall audit.
B4.my_method: Grepped every pipeline/*.py for imports of program_grade / RE_* from research_v205_hybrid.py; read each use site to classify whether the rule JUDGES labels or merely reports.
B4.detail: The 6-script list is exactly right and all 6 import the hand-written table from v205. Caveats on applicability: (1) research_v205_hybrid.py IS the definition site, so 'it uses the rule' is tautological; (2) research_v209_indep_prog.py and research_v210_final3arm.py use the RE_* patterns as FEATURES for a data-driven recalibration and their docstrings explicitly name the contamination ('§258 发现：程序 token 表由评估集标注反推'), so a recall audit is applicable and partly self-served; (3) research_v207_equiv.py already computes L1_prog_recall and L1_model_recall, i.e. a recall comparison exists; (4) research_v206_signif.py uses the rule only as the H2 arm in a three-arm comparison and never as ground truth. So a recall audit is GENUINELY applicable to v208 (which uses program_grade as the oracle to judge human labels) and v209/v210 (which treat the table as calibrated truth), and largely benign in v206/v207/v205.

B5.my_method: Read the three admissibility tests in maps/MULTI_METRIC_ACCEPTANCE.md (T1 trivial-must-fail, T2 chance-comparable, T3 must-not-penalize-correctness) and adjudicated each incident in publish_repo/results/DISCIPLINE_FAILURE.md (the prompt's six: §249/§250/§254/§255/§261/§251) plus the audit's own six (§203/§223/§241/§251/§258/§261), independently, from what each incident actually was.
B5.detail: My independent adjudication gives 1/6 on BOTH the prompt's incident set and the audit's own set -- T3 is written from the §251 adjacent case and catches exactly that one. On the prompt's set I additionally judge NONE as partial: §255 (contaminated comparison arm) is not caught by any of T1/T2/T3 because the admissibility tests are WITHIN-split properties and the leak is CROSS-split; and §261 (narrow rule as truth) is not caught because no test requires an upstream instrument to pass a recall audit. Note the source document DISCIPLINE_FAILURE.md itself says 'Five negative conclusions' (a 5-row table), while the prompt says six by adding §251; either way the coverage verdict is the same. The audit's 'partial' for §241 is defensible but I scored it strictly not-caught since T3 only blocks metrics that reverse, not ones that are too strict.

C1.claim: The label audit discarded a topic-overlap flag that fired on 58% of answered rows.
C1.my_method: Built my OWN topic-overlap measure: character-bigram + latin-token intersection between intent and work_log, over all 11 graded sets (2920 bindings, 2652 answered). Also reproduced the audit's own topic_ratio definition from _labelaudit_signals.py and swept thresholds. Then hand-read the flagged rows.
C1.detail: The discard is clearly JUSTIFIED, and my reproduction is if anything stronger than the audit's number. Under the audit's own topic_ratio definition the flag fires on 64.4% (ratio==0) to 65.3% (ratio<0.10) of answered rows on the 11 sets -- close to their 57.8% and comfortably in the same regime. Under MY independent content-word measure it fires on 11.6%, but hand-reading those 307 flagged rows shows they are overwhelmingly CORRECTLY labelled: 'Godot Engine v4.6...' intent with a root-cause log; '好，麻烦做P0和P1.' with a delivered P0+P1 implementation; '先正确提交代码。' with a crash root-cause found. The flag has near-zero precision under either definition. IMPORTANT: the audit's stated REASON ('Chinese intent and Chinese work-log share few literal tokens') is partly wrong or at least insufficient -- my bigram measure found 31% mean overlap -- the real defect is that low literal overlap is uncorrelated with mislabelling, not that the two texts are lexically disjoint. Finding: the flag was correctly discarded; the audit's stated mechanism is imprecise.

C2.claim: The toolchain audit's hand-written regexes make its 92.6% a LOWER bound.
C2.my_method: Measured the regex families' precision against my hand adjudication of the same 27 rows (B1): the LOOSE (any-family) classifier and the backtick-only classifier both fire on 25/27, but only 9/27 are truly evidence-bearing.
C2.detail: The 'lower bound' claim is backwards. A lower bound would require the regexes to UNDER-detect evidence; in fact they OVER-detect it -- the dominant family (backtick_command) matches any inline code span including purely hypothetical ones ('给 E2E 增加 `wait-idle`', '给 RuntimePathResolver 加 `STRICT` 开关'), so it counts plans as completions. Measured against hand truth the regex precision is 0.36 and the reported rate overstates the true FN rate by 2.8x. Corrected statement: the regex-based 92.6% is an UPPER bound on the token table's false-negative rate; the hand-validated rate is 33.3%. This is the same §262 failure mode the audit was criticising -- an unvalidated narrow instrument treated as truth -- applied to the audit's own metric.

unresolvable_claims: B3 attribution share: I confirm the train/eval gap is real and not a base-rate artifact, but cannot quantify how much is explained by authoring-against-eval vs genuine distribution shift, because the rule's git history is not available and v205 post-dates both datasets by ~18 minutes.
A5 annotator identity (3 people vs 1 person x3): genuinely unresolvable from the files; only batch-level not person-level fingerprints exist.

B1 ground truth: my 9/18 split is one careful human reading with a stated rule, not an expert-annotator gold standard; a second reader could move 2-3 borderline rows ([0] performance-comparison-as-deliverable, [23] query-executed-but-no-product, [25] three endpoints tested) and shift the rate between ~0.22 and ~0.44.
self_limits: My A2 'genuinely no evidence' definition and my B1 'has_evidence' rule are BOTH my own judgement calls. I hand-read only the 27-row NONE population for B1 and a sample of the A2 candidates; the A2 bucket count is definition-dependent (1 to 197 across sensible thresholds), so no single number is THE answer.

My B1 classifier is regex-based like the audit's; my added value is the hand adjudication, and that adjudication is itself a judgement, not ground truth. It is subject to the same D1 discipline I am applying to the audits.

I did not re-run the GLiNER model, so any claim that depends on model outputs (v205's H1/H2 arms, the 0.780 accuracy headline) was not independently reproduced. I verified only the program-rule and label-statistics claims.

B2's anti-monotonicity sweep uses the same strength_confusion.json gold and the same seed(7) as the audit; because the claim is arithmetic and the ordering of the sweep is deterministic given the seed, this is an exact reproduction rather than an independent one. I did not re-derive the confusion matrix from model outputs.
I did not inspect every one of the 11 graded sets for id collisions beyond the families used in A3/B3; the v3-pool separation I found was incidental to the A3 construction.
